text: Rank individual OpenAlex authors by distinct 2021–2024 snapshot works on which they themselves list Columbia University or a covered child institution; include all snapshot work types, break ties deterministically by OpenAlex author ID. Among the 80, link pairs on all shared snapshot works, regardless of those two authors' affiliations on each shared work; edge weight is distinct shared works; retain isolates.

Rank by distinct work_id per resolved author_id after matching each author's own byline position (work_id, author_order) to an explicit affiliation with Columbia University I78577930, Lamont-Doherty I152304114, NASA GISS I116578957, ICAP I4387154024, or CZ Biohub NY I4396570641. Include all snapshot work types and 2021–2024 publication years. Sort by descending count then ascending case-sensitive lexicographic OpenAlex short author_id (string, not numeric suffix); use one-based sequential ranks. Use authors.name for top-80 display names.

Build the induced network on the 80 ranked IDs by joining deduplicated selected (work_id, author_id) bylines across all snapshot works without an endpoint affiliation requirement. Store canonical source_author_id < target_author_id in the same lexicographic order, as an undirected edge with weight equal to distinct shared work IDs. Year-specific node counts are qualifying affiliated works; year-specific edge weights are all shared works. Keep all 80 nodes regardless of degree.

Use T1's rank by distinct personally Columbia/covered-child-affiliated snapshot works and T2's undirected ties based on all shared snapshot works (not restricted to affiliation on the joint work), all work types, 2021–2024 inclusive. Degree counts distinct neighbors within the selected 80; weighted degree sums the raw shared-work counts over those neighbors, counting a work once per incident pair. Components are reachability groups, not disciplines; number components by decreasing size then smallest OpenAlex ID, and mark singleton positions explicitly as display-only.

Use independent 2D NetworkX Fruchterman–Reingold force simulations for the two non-singleton components and square-root shared-work attraction weights to retain tie-strength information while damping very strong ties. Fit each linked component isotropically into a separate screen region; put singleton nodes into a distinct rank-ordered display-only grid. Recommend fixed coordinates, raw shared counts in tooltips, and a neutral styling with isolates differentiated.
